I'm not sure I really understand your point, or that you understand mine. I wasn't suggesting that humans are immune to the laws of physics, that would be ridiculous. We are obviously still complexes of organic macromolecules that require energy taken from the surrounding environment to survive.

What I was saying is that when it comes to natural selection, it no longer functions as simply for those of us in the developed world; those of us that have access to medicine, shelter, readily processed food and other technologies. Natural selection occurs when certain genetic traits give an organism an advantage to existing in a certain environment; these organisms are much more likely to survive and pass on these genes, which accumulate over many thousands of years, presenting as a gradual change in an organism's physiology. To put it more concisely: genetic traits are selected through environmental pressures.

In today's world, millions of people who are born with mutations that give rise to debilitating syndromes, for example, are still able to survive and pass on their genetic code because of our ability to remove many of these environmental pressures through medicine and other technologies. That is what I meant by saying we have all but removed ourselves from the forces of natural selection in the developed world.
